summary: An aborted republication of a stranded committed key leaves filesystem metadata ahead of SQL; removing the key can reclaim a different committed entry’s only blob.
scenario: Generated store contains committed A with old content and committed B with peer content. The fixture removes A/meta.json, verifies a cache miss, and obtains BuildClaim::Acquired through the production API. Republishing A with bytes shared by B reaches a generated SQLite insertion trigger that returns error 1811 after metadata replacement. SQL rolls back to A→old and B→peer with peer refcount 1, while A/meta.json lists peer. Removing A decrements peer to zero, unlinks it, and B becomes a miss. A separate executed case observes that get(A) becomes a hit immediately after the failed replacement.

evidence.point: contains returns false when meta.json is absent even if a committed SQL row remains.
claim_build takes the key lock and returns Acquired on get(None).

Replacement releases and records blob refs in a SQL transaction, atomically replaces meta.json, then inserts/replaces entries and commits. A SQL error rolls back DB changes but not metadata replacement.
Removal reads hash list from filesystem metadata.
After its metadata-content race guard, removal deletes the SQL mapping and decrements metadata hashes; consistency with the mapping is not required.
Expected error 1811; old indexed hash, new filesystem hash; peer_blob_exists=false peer_hit=false; peer survival assertion exits 101.
Expected error 1811; failed replacement produces cache hit=true; no-hit assertion exits 101.

trace: wrapper run_rustc -> claim_build -> get(None) on missing-meta stranded row -> BuildClaim::Acquired -> put_with_compile_time -> put_with_compile_time_policy -> atomic metadata replacement -> entries insertion failure -> implicit SQL rollback -> remove_entry -> remove_entry_attempt -> metadata-based decrement -> peer blob unlink -> get(peer) miss. This connects production APIs at source tier; a full compiler invocation was not executed.

authority.quote: Either the whole entry (with correct refcounts) becomes visible, or none of it does — no refcount drift, no half-written row.

severity: Cache-integrity failure affects a different committed entry sharing replacement bytes; peer reuse is lost and old references leak. No source input/user artifact loss or compiler miscompilation was demonstrated. This requires a stranded committed row, replacement content differing from the old generation, and a SQL failure after metadata replacement. Production frequency and natural stranded-state provenance were not established.
reachability_limit: Fixture explicitly deleted generated metadata. Source comments describe committed-but-stranded rows as a replacement case, but that testimony does not establish a normal production origin. Treat as a confirmed conditional integrity result, not an unconditional admission of a naturally occurring production defect.

summary: Unconditional replacement of a healthy committed key is not reachable through the normal build claim.
checked: Generated healthy entry; claim_build returns Committed, so the caller must restore/bypass publication. Original prior probe directly invoked put without this discriminator.
closed_by: Tier 1: evidence/healthy-claim.log exits 0; tier 2: claim_build source 2565-2578 and wrapper claim handling 4450 onward.
reopens_if: A production caller bypasses claim_build or republishes an entry whose hit was otherwise rejected.

summary: A first-publication SQL insertion failure did not create a committed hit or damage the peer.
checked: Generated B committed, A fresh; insertion ABORT after meta write; contains(A)=false, get(A)=None, remove(A) releases no references, B remains a hit and peer refcount stays 1.
reopens_if: A row exists for A before failure, or another fault cut point changes that rollback outcome.

summary: The two sampled logical-removal SQL errors preserved both committed entries.
checked: Generated A/B entries; BEFORE DELETE entries and BEFORE UPDATE blobs aborts independently; removal reports exact injected error; both get calls succeed and old metadata hash remains.
closed_by: Tier 1: evidence/remove-entry-error.log and remove-blob-error.log exit 0; tier 2: removal commits logical changes before physical cleanup.
reopens_if: Commit-level I/O failure, later cleanup failure, different triggers, or concurrent fault timing changes the outcome.

summary: Successful replacement and later removal preserved the peer.
checked: Same missing-meta stranded state, replacement peer content, no publication trigger; peer refcount becomes 2, removal returns it to 1 and peer remains a hit.
reopens_if: The insertion/commit path errors after filesystem metadata replacement.
